draft.title: The characteristics of religion
card: Religions share four main features: beliefs, sacred texts and stories, ethics, and rituals and ceremonies. Each religion expresses them in its own way.
Beliefs are the teachings a religion holds about what is real and true. Sacred texts and stories are the written or spoken works a tradition treats as holy, and they pass on its beliefs.
Ethics are teachings about how to live and treat others. Rituals and ceremonies are set actions, such as prayers or festivals, through which followers express belief.
The features work together as a whole. Each one supports and gives meaning to the others.
draft.remember: A religion is a whole: its beliefs, texts, ethics and rituals support one another.

a.q: Which statement best shows that the features of a religion work together as a whole?
opts: A ritual acts out a belief that a sacred story tells
Each feature is practised alone, apart from the others
A religion needs only beliefs to count as a religion
Rituals are the only feature that followers need to keep
a.why: A ritual that acts out a belief from a sacred story links three features at once. The option about features being practised alone is wrong because the card says the features support one another.
a.clue: Look for the option that links features to one another.

b.q: Each week, Amira's community gathers to read aloud from its holy book and then shares a meal for those in need. Which two features are shown?
opts: Sacred texts and ethics
Beliefs and sacred stories only
Rituals and ceremonies only
Beliefs and rituals only
b.why: Reading from a holy book is a sacred text in use, and sharing a meal with those in need is ethics, which is how to treat others. Rituals alone is tempting because the gathering is a set action, but the scenario also shows a text and an ethical act.
b.clue: Match each action to a feature: what is read, and what is done for others.

a.best: A ritual acts out a belief that a sacred story tells

problems.detail: The right option is the only one without 'only'. The three distractors all end in 'only', so a student can pick 'Sacred texts and ethics' just by spotting the odd one out.
The clue ('what is read, and what is done for others') maps each action straight onto sacred texts and ethics, which gives the answer away.

A weekly gathering to read aloud from a holy book is itself a ritual or ceremony by the card's definition (a set action through which followers express belief). The scenario therefore shows at least three features, and asking for 'which two' is ambiguous. The why even admits the gathering is a set action.

b.q: Leila's tradition teaches that people should tell the truth and treat others fairly, so she refuses to cheat on a test. Which feature of religion does this show?

Beliefs

Sacred texts and stories
